numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Arrow-backed as_unit conversion used pc.cast(safe=False), which truncates toward zero and silently wraps on int64 overflow: negative durations rounded the wrong way (-93784567890123ns -> s gave -93784s), pre-epoch timestamps crossed the epoch (1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789ns -> s gave 1970-01-01 00:00:00), and out-of-bounds upcasts (year-2600 timestamp[s] -> ns) returned int64-wrapped garbage instead of raising.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Downcasts should floor toward -inf (matching numpy/pandas as_unit): -93784567890123ns -> s should give -93785s, and 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789ns -> s should give 1969-12-31 23:59:59. Out-of-bounds casts should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime (timestamps) or OutOfBoundsTimedelta (durations) rather than wrap.
trigger_conditions: Negative durations or timestamps converted to a coarser resolution (e.g. ns -> s), where truncation toward zero differs from floor toward -inf
Pre-epoch timestamps converted to a coarser resolution
Upcast to a finer resolution that overflows int64 (e.g. year-2600 timestamp[s] -> ns), which previously wrapped silently instead of raising
Existing tests only used positive, in-range values where truncation and floor coincide
oracle_clues: Regression tests added covering negative durations, pre-epoch timestamps, and overflow, matching numpy-backed behavior
Expected behavior described as matching numpy/pandas as_unit flooring and raising OutOfBoundsDatetime/OutOfBoundsTimedelta
Fix uses int64 floor arithmetic (quotient minus one when remainder negative) for downcasts and safe=True casts for upcasts

numerical_characteristics.precision: nanosecond (ns) to second/millisecond/microsecond downcasts; overflow on upcast such as timestamp[s] to ns
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: -93784567890123 ns (about -93784 s) for negative durations; 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789 for pre-epoch timestamps; year 2600 timestamp[s] upcast to ns overflows; duration value 19880899200 s overflows when upcast to ns
category_specific_evidence: Downcast of -93784567890123ns to s gave -93784s before the fix; correct floor result is -93785s
Pre-epoch timestamp 1969-12-31 23:59:59.123456789ns to s gave 1970-01-01 00:00:00 before the fix; correct result is 1969-12-31 23:59:59
Out-of-bounds upcast of year-2600 timestamp[s] to ns silently returned int64-wrapped values instead of raising OutOfBoundsDatetime
Expected formula: floor toward -inf (quotient = i8 / ratio, floored = quotient - 1 when remainder < 0), not truncation toward zero as with pc.cast(safe=False)
Overflow on same/finer-resolution cast must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime/OutOfBoundsTimedelta, as in numpy-backed behavior

Regression tests added: test_as_unit_duration_negative_floors, test_as_unit_timestamp_pre_epoch_floors, test_as_unit_timestamp_overflow_raises (ser of 2600-01-01 to ns), test_as_unit_duration_overflow_raises (duration[s] 19880899200 to ns)
reproduction_risks: The safe=False path was only exercised by positive, in-range values, where truncation and floor coincide, so reproduction must use negative or pre-epoch values to expose the bug
Overflow test requires pyarrow timestamp[s] dtype and pandas OutOfBoundsDatetime import from pandas.errors
Test expectations compare against numpy-backed as_unit results rather than fixed literal values in the passages
